title: UK to deploy fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
summary:
RAF Typhoon fighters will fly defensive missions over cities and infrastructure, in extension of UK support for Riyadh

RAF Typhoon fighters are to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s…
byline: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor

blocks.text: RAF Typhoon fighters are to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s Houthis, flying defensive missions over the country’s cities and critical infrastructure, as western allies step up their intervention in the escalating conflict.

The operation – the most significant military mission signed off by Andy Burnham as prime minister – will involve RAF pilots attempting to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones, after attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities.

An Atlas A400M transport aircraft, capable of transporting heavy equipment, and military advisers will also be provided, in addition to an existing commitment to supply air-to-air refuelling for Saudi fighter jets with an RAF Voyager.

An offensive by the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen that began in September has gradually escalated into a deadly regional conflict, with the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, the backer of Yemen’s officially recognised government.
Earlier this month, 13 people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid international airport in Riyadh, in the deadliest incident in a war that has claimed 19 lives in Saudi Arabia.
Further details of the operation are expected to be communicated to the UK parliament in a written statement shortly.
